newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols firm in Sept, weak in Dec.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols firm in Sept, weak in Dec.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options diverged Tuesday, with September underpinned by steady buying of outright contracts but December dropping two-tenths of a point.
"It is very unusual to see the back month getting slammed and the front month holding firm," said an options trader on the bond floor.
Steady commercial buying of September options, both puts and calls, bolstered volatility in the front month, said an options floor broker.
It hovered at about 7.65 percent throughout the day, up from 7.50 percent the previous session, traders said.
By contrast, December slid to about 8.34 percent from an opening level of 8.55 percent and the previous day's close at 8.65 percent.

Although the September contracts expire in less than three weeks, they retain the bulk of the open interest in options. Heavy rolling of September positions into October and December is expected mid-month.

Large-size trades this session included a German bank's purchase of 2,000 September 114-00 puts and the sale by a U.S. brokerage house of 3,000 September 117-00 covered calls. Earlier in the day, a Wall Street dealer firm also bought 2,000 of the September 114-00 puts.
In the December options, a dealer firm was a seller of 118-00 calls throughout the day.
But traders speculated the decline in December volatility was due more to perceptions that bond futures were likely to stabilize going forward, following Friday's plunge of nearly two full points.
"Local options traders are saying, 'we've had some good moves, now we're due for some sideways action,'" said the floor trader.
Eurodollar volatilities were also steady to lower, with December holding at 9.50 percent and March slipping 0.3 percentage point to 11.0 percent.
